When you wash your hands, soap molecules break down the lipids in the oil, easily removing the oily dirt and germs!
copy.tl:

Kapag nagpapahugas ka, ang mga molekula ng sabon ay nagbabasag ng mga lipid sa mantika, kaya natatanggal ang oily dirt at mga mikrobyo!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagtangtang sa sabon sa oily dirt ug mga mikrobyo?

Kung nagpahugas ka, ang mga molekula sa sabon mo-bungkag sa mga lipid sa mantika, mao nga matanggal ang oily dirt ug mga mikrobyo!

The rich volcanic soil around it gives essential nutrients for the abaca plants to grow!
copy.tl:
Bakit maganda tumubo ang abaca malapit sa Bulkang Bulusan?

Ang masaganang volcanic soil sa paligid nito ay nagbibigay ng essential nutrients para tumubo ang abaca!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga maayo motubo ang abaca duol sa Mount Bulusan?

Ang rich volcanic soil sa palibot niini naghatag ug essential nutrients para motubo ang abaca!

copy.tl: Kailangan ng mga natural na proseso ng halos 500 taon para makabuo ng isang pulgada ng topsoil. Katumbas ito ng tatlong naka-stack na smartphone!
copy.bis: Mogkinahanglan ug natural nga proseso mga 500 ka tuig aron makahimo ug usa ka pulgada nga topsoil. Sama kini sa gibag-on sa tulo ka nagtapok nga smartphone!

copy.tl: Ang araw ay gawa sa plasma, isang superheated state of matter na umaabot ng 15 million degrees Celsius sa core nito!
copy.bis: Ang adlaw kay gawa sa plasma, usa ka superheated state of matter nga moabot og 15 million degrees Celsius sa iyang core!

copy.en:
Why don't planets fly away into deep space?

The Sun's massive gravity constantly pulls planets toward it, keeping them in curved elliptical orbits instead of flying into deep space!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi lumilipad ang mga planeta palayo sa kalawakan?

Ang napakalakas na gravity ng Araw ay humihila sa mga planeta, kaya nananatili sila sa paikot-paikot na elliptical na orbit imbes na lumipad palayo!
copy.bis:
Nganong dili molupad ang mga planeta palayo sa lawom nga kalawakan?

Ang kusog kaayo nga grabidad sa Adlaw kanunay nga nagdani sa mga planeta, mao nga magpabilin sila sa kurbado nga elliptical nga orbit imbes nga molupad palayo!

What is a South Sea pearl actually made of?

The South Sea pearl is a solid mixture composed primarily of microscopic calcium carbonate crystals and conchiolin!
copy.tl:
Ano ang talagang ginawa ng isang South Sea pearl?

Ang South Sea pearl ay isang solid mixture na binubuo mainly ng maliliit na calcium carbonate crystals at conchiolin!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang tinuod nga gihimo sa South Sea pearl?

Ang South Sea pearl usa ka solid mixture nga naglangkob sa microscopic calcium carbonate crystals ug conchiolin!

Just how loud is a rock concert compared to a tiny whisper?

A whisper is 30 decibels and a rock concert is 120 decibels, making the concert one billion times more intense!
copy.tl:
Gaano kalakas ang isang rock concert kumpara sa isang maliit na bulong?

Ang bulong ay 30 decibels at ang rock concert ay 120 decibels, kaya ang concert ay isang bilyong beses na mas intense!
copy.bis:
Unsa kabaskog ang rock concert kumpara sa gamay nga whisper?

Ang whisper kay 30 decibels ug ang rock concert kay 120 decibels, buot pasabot nga ang concert usa ka bilyon ka beses nga mas intense!

copy.tl: Naglalakbay ang liwanag ng 300,000 kilometers per second! Kaya ang sikat ng araw na nakikita mo ngayon ay umalis na sa Araw walong minuto na ang nakalipas.
copy.bis: Naglihok ang kahayag og 300,000 kilometers per second! Mao nga ang kahayag sa adlaw nga imong makita karon miadto na sa adlaw walo ka minuto ang milabay.

Nagpagawas kini og sulfur dioxide gas kung mo-erupt!

Sulfur dioxide gas escapes from Taal Volcano's main crater! This shows how matter exists as an invisible gas at high temperatures.

Ang sulfur dioxide na gas ay lumalabas mula sa pangunahing crater ng Bulkang Taal! Nagpapakita ito kung paano umiiral ang bagay bilang walang nakikitang gas sa mataas na temperatura.

Unsang gas ang mogawas gikan sa Bulkang Taal?

Ang sulfur dioxide nga gas mogawas gikan sa main crater sa Bulkang Taal! Nagpakita kini kung giunsa pag-eksistir ang butang ingon nga dili makita nga gas sa taas nga temperatura.

copy.tl: Ang mga astronaut ng Apollo 11 ay lumapag sa Sea of Tranquility sa Moon, na siyang unang pagbisita ng tao sa ibang celestial body!
copy.bis: Ang mga astronaut sa Apollo 11 milukso sa Sea of Tranquility sa Moon, nga mao ang unang pagbisita sa tawo sa laing celestial body!

What causes ocean tides?

Both the Moon and the Sun cause ocean tides, but the closer Moon has about twice the Sun's tidal effect!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagdudulot ng ocean tides?

Parehong ang Moon at ang Sun ang nagdudulot ng ocean tides, pero dahil mas malapit ang Moon, doble ang tidal effect nito kumpara sa Sun!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang nagmugna og ocean tides?

Ang Moon ug ang Sun pareho nga nagmugna og ocean tides, apan tungod kay mas duol ang Moon, doble ang tidal effect niini kumpara sa Sun!

PAGASA names typhoons using a list of Filipino words, like Yolanda or Rolly, to help communities easily remember and prepare!

Pinangalanan ito gamit ang listahan ng mga salitang Filipino, tulad ng Yolanda o Rolly, para madaling matandaan at mapaghandaan ng mga komunidad!
copy.bis:

Nag-ngalan sila gamit ang lista sa mga pulong nga Filipino, sama sa Yolanda o Rolly, aron sayon ra nga mahinumduman ug mapangandaman sa mga komunidad!

Why does thick honey flow much slower than thin water?

Liquids have different viscosities! Thick honey flows much slower than thin water due to internal friction.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas mabagal dumaloy ang makapal na honey kaysa sa manipis na tubig?

May iba't ibang viscosity ang mga likido! Mas makapal na honey ay mas mabagal dumaloy kaysa sa manipis na tubig dahil sa internal friction.
copy.bis:
Nganong mas hinay molihok ang lapot nga honey kumpara sa manipis nga tubig?

Laing-laing viscosity ang mga likido! Ang lapot nga honey molihok hinay kaayo kumpara sa manipis nga tubig tungod sa internal friction.

assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe properties of solids, liquids, or gases in terms of shape and volume. It focuses on viscosity and appearance, not on the defining properties of states of matter.

Can a liquid look like a solid?

Yes! Pitch is a highly viscous liquid that looks completely solid. It takes an average of ten years for just one single drop to fall!
copy.tl:
Maaari bang magmukhang solid ang isang likido?

Oo! Ang pitch ay napakakapal na likido na mukhang solid. Tumitagal ito ng halos sampung taon bago bumagsak ang isang patak!
copy.bis:
Mahimo bang murag solid ang usa ka likido?

Oo! Ang pitch kay taas kaayo nga viscous nga likido nga murag solid. Moabot ug napulo ka tuig aron mahulog ang usa ka patak!

Where is most of Earth's water hiding?

Over 97% of Earth's water is salty! Most of the remaining freshwater is locked away in glaciers.

Mahigit 97% ng tubig sa Earth ay maalat! Karamihan sa natitirang freshwater ay nakakandado sa mga glacier.

Asa nakatago ang kadaghanan sa tubig sa Yuta?

Kapin sa 97% sa tubig sa Yuta kay asin! Kadaghanan sa nabilin nga freshwater nakakandado sa mga glacier.

copy.en:
What are the historic houses in Vigan made of?

They are built using adobe! It is a solid building material made from compacted clay and volcanic ash.
copy.tl:
Ano ang gamit sa paggawa ng mga makasaysayang bahay sa Vigan?

Ginawa sila gamit ang adobe! Ito ay matibay na materyal na gawa sa pinagsiksik na luwad at volcanic ash.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gigamit sa pagtukod sa mga historic nga balay sa Vigan?

Gitukod kini gamit ang adobe! Kini usa ka lig-on nga materyal nga gihimo gikan sa compacted nga lapok ug volcanic ash.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: keeping your lungs protected
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions lungs but does not identify parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or describe how they work. It only states that an N95 mask filters particles and protects the lungs, which is not direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: keeping your lungs protected
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe how the respiratory system (or any body system) works. It only mentions lung protection from a mask, which is related to respiratory health but does not teach the system's function as required by the competency.

copy.en: Wearing an N95 mask filters out at least 95% of airborne dust and smoke particles, keeping your lungs protected!
copy.tl: Ang pagsusuot ng N95 mask ay humaharang ng hindi bababa sa 95% ng alikabok at usok sa hangin, para protektado ang baga mo!
copy.bis: Ang pagsul-ob og N95 mask nag-filter og dili menos sa 95% sa alikabok ug usok sa hangin, aron maprotektahan ang imong baga!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A cheetah can sprint up to 112 kilometers per hour
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives speed values in km/h but never states that speed is how far an object moves in a given time, nor names the concept of speed. It only provides comparative examples, so it does not directly teach the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A cheetah can sprint up to 112 kilometers per hour
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card compares running speeds of a cheetah and a human. It does not describe outer body parts of animals or their roles in movement and food gathering, so it does not support this living-things competency.

copy.en: A cheetah can sprint up to 112 kilometers per hour — the fastest human runner only reaches about 44 km/h.
copy.tl: Kayang tumakbo ng cheetah nang hanggang 112 kilometro kada oras — ang pinakamabilis na tao ay umaabot lang ng 44 kilometro kada oras.
copy.bis: Ang cheetah makadagan hangtod 112 kilometro kada oras — ang pinakadali nga tawo makaabot lang og 44 kilometro kada oras.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A balut is a fertilized duck egg with a partly developed embryo inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a duck egg and embryo but does not identify or compare groups that give birth to live young versus those that lay eggs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A balut is a fertilized duck egg with a partly developed embryo inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card only notes a partly developed embryo; it does not compare life-cycle stages of mammals, birds, or plants.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A balut is a fertilized duck egg with a partly developed embryo inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies development but does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A balut is a fertilized duck egg with a partly developed embryo inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a flow chart or compare different stages in an animal life cycle.

copy.en:
What's really inside a balut?

A balut is a fertilized duck egg with a partly developed embryo inside, and it's rich in protein and calcium for people who eat it.
copy.tl:
Ano talaga ang laman ng balut?

Ang balut ay fertilized na itlog ng pato na may bahagyang nabuong embryo sa loob, masustansya ito sa protein at calcium para sa taong kumakain nito.
copy.bis:
Unsa gyoy sulod sa balut?

Ang balut kay fertilized nga itlog sa pato nga naay gamay nga nahimong embryo sulod, dato kini sa protein ug calcium para sa tawo nga mokaon niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Binoculars let wildlife researchers watch how animals behave
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions binoculars, which use lenses and prisms, but it does not describe or illustrate reflection or refraction, nor does it involve guided investigations with mirrors, lenses, or prisms. It only states that binoculars help observe animals, so it is related to optics but does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What tool helps scientists watch animals?

Binoculars let wildlife researchers watch how animals behave without getting close enough to disturb them!
copy.tl:
Anong gamit ng scientist sa hayop?

Sa pamamagitan ng binoculars, nakikita ng mga researcher ang galaw ng hayop nang hindi ito nababahala!
copy.bis:
Unsang gamit sa siyentista sa hayop?

Pinaagi sa binoculars, makita sa mga tigdukiduki ang lihok sa hayop nga wala kini nadisturbo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: lower air pressure reduces the boiling point
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that lower air pressure lowers the boiling point of water, not that changes in temperature cause matter to change state. It is about pressure affecting a state change, not the temperature-driven solid-liquid-gas transitions the competency requires.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: water boils at just 68 degrees Celsius
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions boiling (a change of state) but does not describe melting, evaporation, freezing, or condensation, and it does not use diagrams or flowcharts. The focus is on pressure lowering the boiling point, not on describing the processes of changes of state.

copy.en: At the peak of Mount Everest, water boils at just 68 degrees Celsius because lower air pressure reduces the boiling point!
copy.tl: Sa tuktok ng Mount Everest, ang tubig ay kumukulo sa 68°C lamang dahil ang mababang air pressure ay nagpapababa ng boiling point!
copy.bis: Sa tumoy sa Mount Everest, ang tubig mobukal sa 68°C ra tungod kay ubos nga air pressure nagpaubos sa boiling point!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bones are solid organs made mostly of a rigid matrix of calcium phosphate minerals and flexible collagen proteins!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the composition of bones, which is background knowledge for the skeletal system, but it does not describe how the skeletal system works (e.g., support, movement, protection).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bones are solid organs made mostly of a rigid matrix of calcium phosphate minerals and flexible collagen proteins!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions 'rigid' and 'flexible', which are physical properties, but it does not describe the physical properties of solid materials in general or give examples like hard, shiny, or stretchable. It is about bone composition, not a general lesson on solid material properties.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bones are solid organs made mostly of a rigid matrix of calcium phosphate minerals and flexible collagen proteins!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bones are solid organs, but it does not identify the three states of matter (solids, liquids, gases) or teach that matter exists in these states. The word 'solid' is incidental, not instructional for the competency.

copy.en:
What are our bones made of?

Bones are solid organs made mostly of a rigid matrix of calcium phosphate minerals and flexible collagen proteins!
copy.tl:
Ano ang gawa ng mga buto natin?

Ang mga buto ay solid organs na gawa sa rigid matrix ng calcium phosphate minerals at flexible collagen proteins!
copy.bis:
Unsay gihimo sa atong mga bukog?

Ang mga bukog kay solid organs nga gibuhat sa rigid matrix sa calcium phosphate minerals ug flexible collagen proteins!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: overcome gravity in water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions gravity but does not identify it as a non-contact force or explain its predictable effects on materials/objects. The focus is on density and buoyancy, not the nature of gravity as a force.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: decrease its density
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses density affecting floating, which is a property of the object, but it does not explore size, shape, heaviness, material, or surface texture as factors affecting movement. The connection to the competency is only through the general idea of what affects motion.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: overcome gravity in water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific effect of gravity (floating) but does not observe or describe the effects of gravity on the motion of an object in a general or investigative way. It is a single example without explaining the motion outcome or gravity's role.

copy.en:
How does a whale shark float easily?

The whale shark uses an oil-filled liver to decrease its density and overcome gravity in water!
copy.tl:
Paano lumulutang nang madali ang whale shark?

Ang whale shark ay may oil-filled liver para bumaba ang density nito at mapagtagumpayan ang gravity sa tubig!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paglutang sa whale shark nga sayon?

Ang whale shark adunay oil-filled liver aron moubos ang density niya ug mapildi ang gravity sa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: hot gases that cool to deposit bright yellow crystals of solid elemental sulfur
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows a gas-to-solid change (deposition) caused by cooling, but the competency specifically targets changes such as solid to liquid to gas (melting, evaporation). The card does not describe the target state changes or the general principle of temperature-driven state changes in a way that directly supports the listed examples.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: hot gases that cool to deposit bright yellow crystals of solid elemental sulfur
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card illustrates a change of state (gas to solid) but does not use diagrams or flowcharts, and the competency names melting, evaporation, freezing, and condensation—not deposition. The card is only tangentially related to the listed processes.

copy.en:
What bright crystals form from hot gases on Camiguin island?

Volcanic vents on Camiguin island emit hot gases that cool to deposit bright yellow crystals of solid elemental sulfur!
copy.tl:
Anong maliwanag na kristal ang nabubuo mula sa mainit na gas sa Camiguin island?

Ang mga volcanic vent sa Camiguin island ay nagbubuga ng mainit na gas na lumalamig at nag-iiwan ng maliwanag na dilaw na kristal ng solid elemental sulfur!
copy.bis:
Unsay hayag nga kristal ang maporma gikan sa init nga gas sa Camiguin island?

Ang mga volcanic vent sa Camiguin island nagpagawas og init nga gas nga mobugnaw ug magpabilin og hayag nga dilaw nga kristal sa solid nga elemental sulfur!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Jose Rizal utilized chemical changes when developing photographs!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions that chemical changes were used in photography; it does not explain why physical changes are reversible and chemical changes are irreversible, which is the core of G6-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Jose Rizal utilized chemical changes when developing photographs!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the formation of new bonds or the breaking of existing bonds constitutes a chemical change and the formation of a new substance
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions chemical changes but does not explain bond formation/breaking or the formation of a new substance, which is the focus of G9-M-2.

copy.en: Jose Rizal utilized chemical changes when developing photographs! He used light-sensitive silver halide chemicals to make the pictures appear.
copy.tl: Gumamit si Jose Rizal ng chemical changes sa pag-develop ng photographs! Ginamit niya ang light-sensitive silver halide chemicals para lumabas ang mga larawan.
copy.bis: Gigamit ni Jose Rizal ang chemical changes sa pag-develop sa photographs! Gigamit niya ang light-sensitive silver halide chemicals aron makita ang mga litrato.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's an imaginary line of latitude at 23.5 degrees north! It marks the northernmost point where the sun can be directly overhead.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a physical model or use drawings to demonstrate how the tilt of the Earth relative to its orbit around the Sun affects the intensity of sunlight absorbed by different areas of Earth over a year
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines the Tropic of Cancer as a latitude line where the sun can be directly overhead, which is a consequence of Earth's tilt. However, it does not demonstrate or explain how the tilt of the Earth relative to its orbit affects the intensity of sunlight absorbed by different areas over a year, nor does it involve a physical model or drawings as required by the competency.

copy.en:
What is the Tropic of Cancer?

It's an imaginary line of latitude at 23.5 degrees north! It marks the northernmost point where the sun can be directly overhead.
copy.tl:
Ano ang Tropic of Cancer?

Ito ay isang imahinaryong linya ng latitude sa 23.5 degrees north! Ito ang pinakahilagang punto kung saan maaaring direktang tumapat ang araw.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang Tropic of Cancer?

Kini usa ka imahinasyon nga linya sa latitude sa 23.5 degrees north! Kini ang pinakahilagang punto diin ang adlaw direkta nga moabut sa ibabaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A baby coconut sprout eats the soft meat inside its shell for food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a single detail of coconut germination (the sprout using stored food until leaves can photosynthesize). It does not compare life cycles of mammals, birds, and plants, nor does it trace a plant from seed to young plant to mature plant in a way that supports the comparison required by G5-L-6.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: until its green leaves grow big enough to make their own food through photosynthesis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions that leaves eventually make food through photosynthesis. It does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor identify raw materials and products, so it does not directly support G8-L-9.

copy.en: A baby coconut sprout eats the soft meat inside its shell for food -- until its green leaves grow big enough to make their own food through photosynthesis.
copy.tl: Kumakain muna ng laman sa loob ng baluti ang batang usbong ng niyog -- hanggang sa lumaki ang berdeng dahon nito para makagawa na ito ng sariling pagkain sa photosynthesis.
copy.bis: Mokaon una sa unod sulod sa balat ang bata pa nga liso sa lubi -- hangtod modako ang berdeng dahon niini aron makahimo na kini og kaugalingong pagkaon pinaagi sa photosynthesis.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Heavy layers of sediment press down to squeeze water out, forming solid sedimentary rock like sandstone.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the process of compaction forming sedimentary rock. G5-E-2 requires exploring/collecting rocks and describing similarities/differences in features such as texture, color, and grain crystal size. The card does not involve observation, collection, or feature comparison; it only shares the broad topic of rocks.

copy.en:
How does loose dirt turn into solid rock?

Through compaction! Heavy layers of sediment press down to squeeze water out, forming solid sedimentary rock like sandstone.
copy.tl:
Paano nagiging solid rock ang malambot na lupa?

Sa compaction! Ang mabibigat na patong ng sediment ay pinipiga pababa para maalis ang tubig, bubuo ng solid sedimentary rock tulad ng sandstone.
copy.bis:
Giunsa paghimo sa loose dirt nga solid rock?

Pinaagi sa compaction! Ang bug-at nga layers sa sediment nagpress down aron ma-squeeze ang tubig, moporma og solid sedimentary rock sama sa sandstone.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It floats because its overall density is less than water's density!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains floating in terms of density, which is a property of matter, but it does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. The competency's core definition is not taught or supported.

copy.en:
Why does a mature buko float in water?

It floats because its overall density is less than water's density!
copy.tl:
Bakit lumulutang ang mature na buko sa tubig?

Lumulutang ito dahil mas mababa ang kabuuang density nito kaysa sa density ng tubig!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga molutaw ang hamtong nga buko sa tubig?

Molutaw kini kay ang kinatibuk-ang density niini mas ubos kay sa density sa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The foam inside is less dense than water, providing enough buoyancy to keep your head safely above the surface!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains buoyancy and density, which are not about the movement of objects. The competency focuses on factors affecting movement (size, shape, heaviness, material, surface texture). The card does not describe how these factors affect movement; it only explains why a life jacket floats. This is a related physics concept but does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en:
How does a life jacket keep you floating?

The foam inside is less dense than water, providing enough buoyancy to keep your head safely above the surface!
copy.tl:
Paano ka pinapanatiling lumutang ng life jacket?

Ang foam sa loob ay mas magaan kaysa tubig, nagbibigay ng sapat na buoyancy para mapanatiling nakalutang ang ulo mo!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpabilin sa life jacket nga molutaw ka?

Ang foam sulod mas magaan kaysa tubig, naghatag og igo nga buoyancy aron mapabilin nga nakalutaw ang imong ulo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Frost is water vapor changing directly into solid ice crystals!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes deposition (vapor to solid), which is not among the processes named in the competency (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation), and it does not use diagrams or flowcharts as the competency requires.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Frost is water vapor changing directly into solid ice crystals!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example of a temperature-related state change, but the competency focuses on solid to liquid to gas transitions; deposition is not directly covered.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Frost is water vapor changing directly into solid ice crystals!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes: a. solid → liquid → vapor, and b. vapor → liquid → solid
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a vapor-to-solid change, which is related to the competency's vapor → liquid → solid sequence, but it does not explain particle arrangement or energy changes as required.

copy.en:
What is frost on mountain grass?

Frost is water vapor changing directly into solid ice crystals! It forms on high altitude mountain grass without becoming liquid water first.
copy.tl:
Ano ang hamog sa damo ng bundok?

Ang hamog ay singaw ng tubig na nagiging solid ice crystals nang direkta! Ito ay nabubuo sa matataas na bundok na damo.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang hamog sa sagbot sa bukid?

Ang hamog kay singaw sa tubig nga nag-direct nga nahimong solid ice crystals! Kini motubo sa sagbot sa taas nga bukid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When salt dissolves in water, it doesn't disappear! It just breaks into microscopic ions that stay evenly mixed in the liquid.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes dissolution and the even mixing of salt ions in water, but it never names the solute or solvent or identifies their roles in a solution. It shares vocabulary about solutions but does not directly support the competency's required identification of solute and solvent roles.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When salt dissolves in water, it doesn't disappear! It just breaks into microscopic ions that stay evenly mixed in the liquid.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a dissolved salt mixture as evenly mixed, which is characteristic of a uniform mixture, but it does not describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, nor does it contrast solutions with suspensions. It only touches on the idea of even mixing without addressing the competency's classification or examples.

copy.en: When salt dissolves in water, it doesn't disappear! It just breaks into microscopic ions that stay evenly mixed in the liquid.
copy.tl: Kapag natunaw ang asin sa tubig, hindi ito nawawala! Nagiging maliliit na ions lang ito na pantay na nakakalat sa likido.
copy.bis: Kung matunaw ang asin sa tubig, dili kini mawala! Mo-break lang kini into microscopic ions nga evenly distributed sa tibuok liquid mixture.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earthquakes are caused by the sudden movement of tectonic plates deep underground!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models or illustrations to explain how movements along faults generate earthquakes and identify and explain which types of faults are most likely to occur in the Philippines and explain why
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a general cause of earthquakes (tectonic plate movement) but does not use models or illustrations, does not explain how movements along faults generate earthquakes, and does not identify Philippine fault types as required by the competency.

copy.en: Earthquakes are caused by the sudden movement of tectonic plates deep underground! They are not caused by severe weather conditions.
copy.tl: Ang lindol ay dulot ng biglaang paggalaw ng tectonic plates sa ilalim ng lupa! Hindi ito dahil sa severe weather conditions.
copy.bis: Ang linog tungod sa kalit nga paglihok sa tectonic plates ilawom sa yuta! Dili kini tungod sa severe weather conditions.
